```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5)
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(herminR)
```

Eq. (4) of Otava and Mylona (2020) sums the per-term maximal contributions (L1); only L1 is a
maximal change of the response. L2 and L-infinity are alternative summaries
(referee W3): L-infinity reports the single largest contribution, L2 sits in
between.

```{r}
b <- c(x1 = 0.9, x2 = 0.3, "x2^2" = 0.3, "x1:x2" = 0.05, "x2:x3" = 0.3, x3 = 0.1)
cmp <- mpi_compare_norms(b, abs = TRUE)
cmp$l1
attr(cmp, "rank_agreement")
plot(cmp)
```

Factor `x2` is influential through several moderate terms, so it ranks
higher under L1 than under L-infinity.

Each panel is scaled by its own maximum, so the plot compares the *pattern*
of influence between norms; the values are not comparable in magnitude across
panels, and only L1 is an attainable change of the response.
